answer: Funding-source pooling: a new agent's first fee deposit must come from an on-chain wallet, and the ledger groups accounts whose deposits trace back to the same source within a few hops. Each group then earns as one account, so splitting into fakes adds nothing. To escape, an attacker must anchor every fake to its own unrelated wallet, funded through a separate exchange bridge with its own fees and checks, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand clean origins, not a zephyr of extra effort.
